profile.name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A.
profile.summary: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A., together with its subsidiaries, provides various financial services in Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company offers traditional retail, wholesale, investment, and transaction banking. It also engages in financial, insurance, asset management, and capital markets businesses, as well as digital banking. The company was formerly known as Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, S.A. and changed its name to Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. in January 2000. Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. was founded in 1857 and is headquartered in Bilbao, Spain.

streams.description: BBVA is a bank providing retail, wholesale, investment, and transaction banking, plus financial, insurance, asset management, and capital markets services across Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, Europe, the US, and Asia. It earns money primarily from net interest income and fees and commissions, with additional net trading income. In 1H2026, net interest income was €15.16 billion and fees and commissions were €4.57 billion, lifting gross income to €21.16 billion.
streams.notes: Net interest income and fees and commissions grew year-over-year in 1H2026, supported by loan growth of 17.7% at constant exchange rates.
streams.geography: The company reports business areas including Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, Rest of Business, and Corporate Center.

trends.claim: Mexican bank deposits and lending regained momentum in June 2026, with credit growing 3.0% and deposits 3.1% in real annual terms.
trends.why: Higher loan and deposit volumes expand BBVA Mexico's net interest income base.
trends.quote: In June 2026, bank deposits and lending in Mexico showed greater momentum, driven by time deposits and consumer credit.
trends.size_basis: 3.0% credit and 3.1% deposit real annual growth; no absolute size.
trends.impact_basis: Mexico NII is core; NII is 71.6% of revenue.
trends.theme_definition: Bank deposits and lending expand, supporting net interest income for banks.

trends.claim: Mexican non-financial private sector credit slowed to 1.3% real annual in April 2026, with corporate lending negative for a fourth quarter.
trends.why: Slower loan growth limits BBVA Mexico's interest-earning asset expansion.
trends.quote: In April 2026, the outstanding credit to the non-financial private sector continued to slow, reaching 1.3% in real annual terms
trends.size_basis: 1.3% real annual credit growth; no absolute size.
trends.impact_basis: Mexico loan growth feeds NII, 71.6% of revenue.
trends.theme_definition: Demand for commercial credit from businesses rises or falls, affecting bank loan growth.

trends.claim: Euro area banks reported moderate net tightening of corporate credit standards in Q2 2026, with a net 7% of banks tightening.
trends.why: Tighter credit standards restrain loan supply and volume growth in BBVA's European markets.
trends.quote: euro area banks reported a moderate net tightening of credit standards for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of banks of 7%
trends.size_basis: Net 7% of banks tightening; no absolute size.
trends.impact_basis: European corporate lending is a minority of BBVA's NII.
trends.theme_definition: Banks tighten credit standards for commercial loans, restraining loan supply and volume.

trends.claim: European SMB banking customers generate up to 12 times more annual revenue than consumer customers, per Visa study in September 2026.
trends.why: Capturing SMB primary relationships lifts fee and interest revenue per customer.
trends.quote: Small business banking customers generate up to 12 times more annual revenue for financial institutions than traditional consumer customers in Europe
trends.speed_basis: September 2026 study; opportunity not yet realized.
trends.impact_basis: SMB is a material but minority customer segment.
trends.theme_definition: Small and medium businesses reconsider primary banking relationships, creating share-shift opportunities.

trends.claim: Mexico's Banxico and CNBV proposed phased caps on credit and debit card interchange fees in August 2026.
trends.why: Lower interchange fees reduce card payment fee revenue for BBVA Mexico.
trends.quote: proposed updated regulations establishing phased caps on credit and debit card interchange fees
trends.size_basis: No market size; caps at 1.30% and MX$10.80.
trends.impact_basis: Card fees are part of 21.6% fee revenue; Mexico is key.
trends.theme_definition: Regulators cap card interchange fees, reducing issuer payment fee revenue.

trends.claim: Stablecoins backed by new US legislation are emerging as a disruptive force in payments as of July 2026.
trends.why: Stablecoin payments could bypass bank rails and erode card and payment fee income.
trends.quote: The payments landscape also seems to be at a crossroads. Stablecoins, backed by the new Guiding and Establishing National Innovation
trends.speed_basis: New legislation and emerging adoption; not yet in reported numbers.
trends.impact_basis: Threatens payment fees, 21.6% of BBVA revenue.
trends.theme_definition: Stablecoins enable payments outside bank rails, threatening bank payment fees.

trends.claim: Nonbank competition is forcing banks to defend margins and diversify fee income as of July 2026.
trends.why: Nonbanks compete for loans, deposits, and payments, pressuring BBVA's spread and fee income.
trends.quote: Banks could be forced to defend margins, diversify fee income, and prepare for increased competition from nonbank entities.
trends.impact_basis: Affects both NII and fees, most of BBVA revenue.
trends.theme_definition: Nonbank financial firms compete with banks for loans, deposits, and payments.

trends.claim: McKinsey's 2026 review warns fintechs and AI-driven disintermediation threaten banks' control of client relationships.
trends.why: Loss of customer ownership can reduce cross-sell and fee income across BBVA.
trends.quote: warns that a new generation of fintechs, AI-driven disintermediation, and shifting customer trust threaten banks' control of client relationships.
trends.impact_basis: Threatens customer relationship across all revenue streams.
trends.theme_definition: AI and fintechs disintermediate banks, threatening control of customer relationships.

trends.claim: Global FX daily trading volumes reached USD 9.6 trillion in 2025, supporting trading revenue in 2026.
trends.why: Higher FX volumes increase client flow and trading income for BBVA's markets business.
trends.quote: daily trading volumes reaching USD 9.6 trillion in 2025
trends.size_basis: USD 9.6 trillion daily FX volume in 2025.
trends.impact_basis: Net trading income share not disclosed; material but minority.
trends.theme_definition: Foreign exchange trading volumes grow, supporting bank trading revenue.

trends.claim: Commercial banks face pressure on spread income as loan repricing continues and funding-cost cuts run out in 2026.
trends.why: Narrower spreads directly reduce BBVA's largest revenue stream, net interest income.
trends.quote: continued repricing of loans and other earning assets is likely to increase pressure on spread income
trends.speed_basis: July 2026 report; pressure expected as rates stabilize.
trends.theme_definition: Falling rates and loan repricing compress bank net interest margins.

trends.claim: Digital transformation remains the top strategic focus for banks in 2026, driving technology spending.
trends.why: Higher technology spend raises BBVA's cost base while potentially improving efficiency and distribution.
trends.quote: digital transformation remains the top focus
trends.impact_basis: Affects operating expenses, not directly revenue.
trends.theme_definition: Banks increase technology spending on digital transformation and AI.

dropped.claim: Fixed income markets saw record trading volumes and AI-driven change in 2026, reshaping bond trading.
dropped.why: Higher volumes lift trading revenue, but nonbank liquidity providers and AI pressure bank market share.
dropped.quote: record trading volumes, the rise of non-bank liquidity providers, and rapid advances in artificial intelligence reshape how bonds are traded.
dropped.speed_basis: 2026 report calls it a tipping point.
dropped.impact_basis: Net trading income share not disclosed; material but minority.
dropped.theme_definition: Trading volumes and volatility lift sales and trading revenue for banks.
